closed_notes.conclusion: YES - the editable announcement text IS saved to the server via a specific message id (primary-static). Click 0x43E4BA: btn2 (this+0x108) press -> test [this+0x1CC] (Win32 edit control handle) -> GetWindowTextA([this+0x1CC], stack buf, 0xFA0) -> line-split loop 0x468BF0 (delim 0xA), each line appended via 0x45DC70(0x8AB7A8, dst, line, 0x8B187C). If accumulator non-empty: state byte [this+0x1D0]==0 -> 0x4524D0 (msg id 0x411, guild level/rank edit mode); [this+0x1D0]!=0 -> 0x4524A0 (msg id 0x410, announcement mode). Each builder: 0x452940 writes a 12-byte header at game+0x18 (dword 0, msg id word at +4; push 0x411 @0x4524DF / push 0x410 @0x4524AF, zero words), then 0x451E60(game, header, text): header copied to game+0x24, seq = [game+0x14] % 9, sprintf '#%d%s%s!' (0x47C840) / '#%d%s!' (0x47C800, null-text path) into game+0x2044, then send([game+0x6044], buf, len) via 0x468098 = jmp [0x476340] (IAT thunk; WS2_32.dll import descriptor 120, slot 0x476340 = 9th IAT entry, value 0x80000013 = ordinal 19 = send).

Banner content = guild/system announcement lines from the game object's singly-linked list (game+0xEC for the show path / game+0xBC for the hide path; node+4 string, node+0xC next), joined with CR LF (0x47BB4C) into the 0x4E2-dword stack buffer via 0x45DC70(0x8AB7A8, buf, line, 0x8B187C) at 0x425A80-0x425AAC / 0x425B7E-0x425BAA, then SetWindowTextA([0x7773CC], buf) at 0x425ABB-0x425AC4 / 0x425BAC-0x425BC2. The banner text control 0x7773CC is a Win32 window filled at show/hide time.

Both guild-window banner buttons dispatch window id 0xF through the SAME visibility dispatcher 0x42ADB0(winmgr 0x7243A4, id 0xF) at 0x425A1F (show) / 0x425B1E (hide) that serves the notice window (id 15); the banner object 0x777200 is constructed with base ctor 0x423E80 at frame 602 (show, [0x7773D0]=1) / 601 (hide, [0x7773D0]=0).
